data.title: ‘Only 5 other times this decade’ – Why Bitcoin’s latest drop stands out
data.description:
The Binance hack has reignited discussions about Bitcoin’s [BTC] ability to recover from major security incidents and financial crises. While the latest breach triggered significant selling pressure, historical data suggests that Bitcoin has often demonstrated resilience following similar events.

According to an infographic shared by Rand Group, Bitcoin has historically recorded substantial gains in the 12 months following major crypto-related disasters. For instance, following the Mt. Gox hack in November 2011, BTC gained approximately 500% over the next year.

Similarly, Bitcoin rallied 160% after the January 2015 post-Mt. Gox collapse and 125% following the December 2018 crypto winter bottom.

The recovery was even stronger after the March 2020 COVID-19 market crash, with BTC gaining approximately 1,100% over the subsequent 12 months. Meanwhile, Bitcoin advanced 130% in the year following the November 2022 FTX collapse.

Execs weigh in on the same

David Lawant, head of research for Anchorage, also echoed the same when he said,

Historically, bitcoin has treated hacks and solvency events very differently: thefts tend to be absorbed within hours, while insolvencies are not.

According to his analysis, cryptocurrency thefts are often absorbed by the market within hours, whereas exchange failures and insolvencies tend to create more prolonged uncertainty.

His data examines Bitcoin’s price movements during the first 8.5 hours following selected incidents, separating exchange hacks, bridge and protocol exploits, and financial collapses. Lawant also argued that such incidents have limited predictive value for Bitcoin’s longer-term direction, which depends more heavily on the broader market cycle.

Not everyone shares the same sentimnet

However, opposing the above observations, Adam Livingston, Vice President, Investments at Strive, noted that Bitcoin experienced a 6.9% decline between the 29th and 30th of October, following the Binance-related panic.

Against its relatively low 30-day volatility of 1.3%, this represented a 5.3-standard-deviation move. It ranked among the most extreme two-day declines since 2020.

He added,

A drop this deep out of a market this quiet has happened only 5 other times this decade.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin has historically recorded substantial gains in the 12 months following major crypto-related disasters.
  • An exec also argued that such incidents have limited predictive value for Bitcoin’s longer-term direction.

data.title: Ethereum whales withdraw $29M despite bearish signals – Will ETH recover?
data.description:
Ethereum [ETH] whales have intensified their accumulation activity despite broader market weakness, withdrawing millions in ETH from exchanges. As per Lookonchain, two whale wallets received 13,002 ETH, worth roughly $29.09 million, from FalconX and OKX.

Specifically, one whale received 9,625 ETH worth nearly $21.57 million from FalconX, while a newly created wallet withdrew 3,377 ETH worth approximately $7.52 million from OKX.

These significant ETH withdrawals highlighted a growing interest among the large investors despite Ethereum’s recent price weakness.

Beyond the reported whale transfers, Ethereum’s broader exchange activity revealed token withdrawals despite prevailing market uncertainty. At the time of reporting, ETH  had recorded around -$35.45 million in Spot Netflow, according to CoinGlass data.

The negative reading implied withdrawals exceeded deposits, extending the broader trend of ongoing exchange outflows. The latest reading notably followed several considerable withdrawal spikes throughout October, an activity that could reduce immediately available selling supply.

However, these outflows are yet to translate into a meaningful price recovery, leaving Ethereum vulnerable to further declines.

Why are Ethereum traders turning increasingly bearish?

Contrastingly, while the Spot exchange withdrawals suggested potential accumulation, Ethereum’s derivatives market, on the other hand, reflected an opposite shift in trader positioning. CoinGlass highlighted that ETH’s OI-Weighted Funding Rate rapidly declined to -0.0097% as of writing.

Notably, the decline marked a sharp reversal from the predominantly positive funding rates recorded throughout the month of October. The reversal meant that the short traders paid long traders, highlighting growing demand for bearish exposure across leveraged positions.

Furthermore, the decline also suggested that the market participants highly anticipated further downside despite substantial whale withdrawals.

However, it is worth noting that the negative funding alone could not validate additional losses, particularly in case renewed buying triggers short liquidations.

Could $2,200 support spark ETH’s next rebound?

Ethereum’s daily chart structure highlighted a persistent bearish pressure as the token traded around $2,240 at press time, within a descending channel.

Notably, the bears had already pushed Ethereum beneath the $2,300 price level, weakening its previous support structure. More importantly, the price subsequently approached the $2,200 potential support, where buyers faced another crucial test.

The RSI indicator, meanwhile, dropped to 29.78 into oversold territory, implying intense selling pressure. Additionally, the MACD indicator  also maintained a bearish outlook below its signal line with its negative histogram confirming that sellers continued controlling the broader trend.

Ultimately, Ethereum’s $29.09 million whale accumulation and persistent exchange outflows offered potential recovery signals, but the prevailing bearish conditions continued limiting immediate recovery attempts.

For a sustained price rebound,  buyers would need to defend the $2,200 support and reclaim the $2,300 price level.

Final Summary

  • Ethereum whales withdrew $29.09 million in ETH as exchange outflows continued.
  • ETH approached $2,200 support, where buyers could likely attempt a recovery despite bearish indicators.

data.title: XRP exchange reserves drop by 250M tokens – Is a price recovery ahead?
data.description:
XRP exchange reserves have dropped across major trading platforms, with Binance recording its lowest holdings since December 2022 amid sustained withdrawals.

Between the 28th and 30th of October, Binance reserves reportedly declined 8.18%, dropping from 2.69 billion to 2.47 billion XRP. Additionally, Bybit, on the other hand,  registered a 6.54% decline, losing 20 million XRP as reserves fell to 286 million.

Furthermore, Bithumb followed with a 10 million XRP reduction, bringing its holdings to 1.837 billion XRP. The three exchanges combined lost 250 million XRP, potentially reducing the supply readily available for selling.

This broader reserve decline raised questions about whether the shrinking exchange supply could support XRP’s price recovery.

Spot outflows reinforce the declining reserve trend

In addition to declining reserves, XRP‘s Spot market experienced continued exchange outflows, further signaling the withdrawal trend. According to CoinGlass, XRP had registered $5.78 million in spot net outflows at the time of writing.

Notably, the netflows were negative for most of the recent trading period, with occasional inflows. This persistent withdrawal reduces exchange-held balances, potentially limiting the amount of tokens available for immediate selling.

However, the continued outflows didn’t necessarily signal higher demand, especially given the headwind of XRP’s recent losses.

XRP’s NVT collapse signals changing network activity

Meanwhile, XRP’s on-chain valuation metrics witnessed a drastic change as the exchange reserves kept declining.

The Network Value to Transactions (NVT) ratio plunged 54.77% over 24 hours as of writing, reaching 54.69. The drastic drop suggested that transactions were growing stronger than XRP’s prevailing market capitalization.

This development implied an expanding network utilization relative to valuation, even though the ratio alone could not confirm undervaluation.

More importantly, the higher relative transaction activity provided another possible basis for recovery, alongside the declining exchange reserves. However, XRP still had to gain more buying momentum to capitalize on these moves and push prices higher.

XRP defends support, but bears threaten recovery

Despite the supportive supply-side developments, XRP’s technical structure continued reflecting bearish pressure following its recent decline.

On the daily timeframe chart, the bulls decisively defended the $1.23 support level, allowing XRP to rebound toward $1.24. The Relative Strength Index indicator, however, remained weak at 36.55 at press time, below its Moving Average of 40.19.

Furthermore, the Money Flow Index (MFI) stabilized around 42.31, implying that buying pressure was yet to regain dominance. However, XRP’s declining exchange reserves and persistent outflows introduced potential support for a recovery attempt. 

The weak technical indicators continued threatening immediate gains, but maintaining the $1.2352 could help buyers challenge higher price levels.

Final Summary

  • XRP exchange reserves declined by 250 million tokens across Binance, Bybit, and Bithumb.
  • XRP defended $1.23 support, but weak indicators threatened a stronger price recovery.

data.title: CLARITY Act back in the spotlight after $6.3B Binance hack — Here’s why!
data.description:
The $6.3 billion Binance hack, the largest crypto security incident on record, has sparked fresh debate over cryptocurrency regulations in the United States, particularly the need for stronger safeguards for crypto exchanges.

According to Senator Cynthia Lummis, the incident highlights why the proposed CLARITY Act is important for the industry’s future.

Lummis blames the CLARITY Act setback

The Senator argued that the legislation would have provided crypto firms with legal clarity to freeze suspicious transactions as soon as law enforcement agencies flagged them. This would have allowed exchanges to respond immediately to potential security threats, rather than lose valuable time navigating regulatory uncertainty.

Lummis added, 

Every minute lost is money gone for good.

Lummis also warned that hackers stole more than $6 billion in less than four hours, making the incident larger than the previous two biggest crypto thefts combined — the $3.5 billion LuBian hack in December 2020 and the $1.4 billion Bybit exploit in February 2025.

CFTC Chairman stresses on new crypto regulations

At the same time, CFTC Chair Mike Selig also used the incident to reinforce the need for a federal registration framework for crypto exchanges. He argued that offshore exchanges lack the cybersecurity safeguards expected of regulated U.S financial markets.

However, his remarks were focused on vulnerabilities in supporting infrastructure, such as an individual’s laptop, rather than weaknesses in blockchain networks or smart contracts. 

Additionally, he also highlighted how blockchain transparency could help regulators trace stolen funds, even when hackers use privacy tools such as Tornado Cash. 

Selig went on to say, 

I think the fact that we can trace transactions on-chain, even when some of these technologies are used to obfuscate that, gives us a lot of potential as a regulator to be really a cop on the beat.

This is evidence that the Binance hack is particularly alarming. Especially since the amount affected already exceeds the combined value of the next nine largest crypto hacks, according to Glassnode. 

Crypto market faces the brunt

Here, it’s worth pointing out that the impact has also extended beyond just security concerns, weighing on market sentiment and liquidity.

According to DefiLlama, DeFi Total Value Locked (TVL) dropped by 5.3% on 30th October to $83.95 billion, its lowest level since 21st August. Stablecoin supply also declined to $296.6 billion, remaining below the $300 billion-mark since 24th October.

Meanwhile, around $1.5 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated as Bitcoin [BTC] briefly fell to $76,400, triggering widespread selling across major cryptocurrencies.

While Pepe [PEPE], Sky [SKY], and Bitcoin Cash [BCH] posted gains, riskier assets such as MemeCore [M], Ethena [ENA], and Pump.fun [PUMP] recorded significant losses.

Therefore, going forward, $76,400 remains a crucial support level for Bitcoin, while reclaiming $80,000 could signal improving market sentiment. On the other hand, a break below $76,000 could extend the broader risk-off trend.

However, with Binance expecting to resume withdrawals within 48 hours (from the day the hack was reported), hope remains.

Final Summary

  • Senator Lummis is the latest to comment on the Binance hack and what could have been done to prevent it. 
  • DeFi TVL dropped by 5.3% to $83.95 billion, while stablecoin supply also fell to $296.6 billion.

data.title: How can PEPE traders take advantage of conflicting momentum signals?
data.description:
At the time of writing, PEPE was down 2.50% in the last 24 hours, its performance noticeably worse than other leading memecoins. For its part, Dogecoin [DOGE] was down by only 0.94%, while Shiba Inu [SHIB] gained by 1.13%.

And yet, the memecoin has rallied by 7.42% over the past week. In fact, Glassnode data also showed that the memecoin sector, as a whole, has shed 3.1% of its value over the past week, less than BTC’s 4.4% or ETH’s 5.9%.

Does PEPE have a longer-term bullish bias, and should swing traders and investors be looking to buy? Here’s what you need to know!

PEPE bulls battle for control of Value Area High

The 1-day chart revealed a bullish swing structure in place. The key levels to watch were $0.0000032 and $0.00000536. A daily session close above $0.00000536 would confirm a bullish trend continuation.

Within this swing move, the Fixed Range Volume Profile tool was used.

It plotted the Value Area Low and High at $0.00000377 and $0.00000491, meaning 70% of the trading volume since 11th September, when the impulse move began, has taken place within these two levels. This also makes them important horizontal levels to watch.

The A/D indicator fell to new lows following the heavy selling on 29th October. Meanwhile, the Awesome Oscillator stayed above the zero line.

These conflicting signals did not seem to subtract from the overall bullish price bias PEPE showed on the daily timeframe. However, ideally, buyers would want to see sustained demand to keep the uptrend going.

PEPE swing traders can maintain a bullish bias

Over the past week, PEPE has oscillated between $0.0000042 and $0.0000056, and at the time of writing, was at the mid-range level. The technical indicators were neutral, with a slight bearish leaning from the Awesome Oscillator.

Traders and long-term investors can stay bullish given the daily timeframe structure, but should be prepared for a price dip toward $0.0000044 or even $0.0000038. Especially if Bitcoin faces intense selling pressure.

Final Summary

  • PEPE has shed more value in the past 24 hours than some of the larger crypto memecoins.
  • Swing traders and investors can maintain a bullish bias as the price challenges the VAH once again.

data.title: Bitcoin fear hits August lows – Why BTC traders are watching $73K
data.description:
Fear across the market following the recent Binance hack is understandable.

In just 24 hours, market sentiment has taken a sharp hit. The Fear & Greed Index has fallen to its lowest point since mid-August to 30 (Fear) from 51 (Neutral). This comes amid the $6.3 billion Binance exploit, adding pressure to an already weak market. Bitcoin dropped 4-5%, touching a six-week low near $76,500 and Ethereum falling below $2,200. Meanwhile, over $1.6 billion in positions were liquidated on the market.

Against this backdrop, AMBCrypto’s latest report starts to make more sense. The largest hack in crypto history has hit the biggest exchange in the space, but Binance is showing signs it is taking it well. Out of the $6.3 billion drained, $3 billion has been frozen, and the rest is being made up by the SAFU fund.

Backing this up, CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost highlighted the trend in the chart above: 

Despite the large exploit, the impact on Binance’s reserve was not too severe. BTC’s value dropped by 3.1%, ETH by 8.5%, XRP by 8%, and USDT by 6.3%. It appears that the shock has been absorbed, keeping the broader impact on users relatively limited.

In this context, the fear could cause an ideal setup for the strong hands to “buy the dip.” As Bitcoin absorbs post-hack selling pressure and weak hands get shaken out, momentum could shift towards a recovery in the $90k range. But the key question is: Do on-chain metrics support this bullish setup? 

Bitcoin’s fear signals align with on-chain buying pressure

Bitcoin’s [BTC] on-chain metrics could reveal whether strong hands are stepping in. 

The latest selloff has triggered a major leverage flush, with BTC falling below $76,000 and ETH slipping under $2,200. In the last 24 hours, over $1.54 billion worth of leveraged positions were liquidated, indicating a large weak-hand shakeout. However, there was also significant net outflows from exchanges, as over 23,600 BTC moved out of exchanges, hinting at continued accumulation despite broader market fear.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin’s Coinbase Premium Index has reached a 4-year low, last seen in November 2022 when the FTX collapse occurred. Interestingly, this was also the time that Bitcoin formed a market bottom. Although it is too early to tell if it is reversing, there are some parallels to suggest Bitcoin could be nearing another accumulation phase.

In short, Bitcoin’s Fear & Greed Index could be masking a shift in underlying market sentiment. 

With on-chain data suggesting accumulation and Binance reserves appearing to recover, selling pressure appears to be cooling off. This puts a potential shift from distribution to a move towards accumulation back in focus, setting the stage for a broader market recovery.

If this trend holds, Bitcoin could continue to hold up well at the key $73k support level ahead of some major macro events.

Final Summary

data.title: Wall Street’s Black Friday — Is a 2022-style crypto winter brewing?
data.description:
November is kicking off with unprecedented levels of market volatility.

The past 24 hours have been one big bloodbath. Tech stocks have been hit particularly hard. Over the last 24 hours, markets in the U.S, Japan, South Korea, China and Taiwan have combined to wipe $1.7 trillion off their market cap. This, after a flurry of earnings reports kicked off the “AI bubble” narrative again. 

The key takeaway? The market got a reality check. For instance, Alphabet lost more than 12% of its market value, highlighting just how quickly sentiment can turn when AI expectations collide with earnings reality.

However, it is the timing of this sell-off that is adding another layer of pressure to the crypto market.

According to the Kobeissi Letter, the probability of a Democratic sweep in next week’s U.S mid-term elections has risen by 7% to a record high of 72% over the last 2 days. This, as markets continue to accelerate their decline, adding another layer of macroeconomic uncertainty for the crypto market.

This leaves us with high rates, a falling stock market, $100+ oil prices, and rising CPI, PPI, and PCE inflation. Next week is going to be interesting, to say the least. 

However, the market isn’t entirely bearish just yet. 

Crypto’s 2022 playbook returns as market volatility builds

It’s been over a year since the October 2025 crash knocked down risk assets.

Bitcoin is still down over 30% from its pre-crash high of $126K. Considering the FUD surrounding U.S mid-terms, the Binance hack and recent tech sell-off, it seems the market still has a long way to go before any real recovery. This puts the question of whether crypto has found its bottom back in focus. 

Notably, the 2022 cycle could offer some clues. Back then, the FTX collapse was just about a year after BTC’s November 2021 high, lining up with the cycle bottom in late Q4 2022, when BTC dropped to $16K. What followed was a 155% rally, followed by another 120% run, pushing Bitcoin close to $108K by 2024.

So, could the ongoing volatility be setting crypto up for a 2022-style cycle?

Based on historical trends, Bitcoin falling below $80K and the overall market sell-off could allude to later phases of a crypto bottom. With macro uncertainty continuing to build, the market could be heading into the final stage of capitulation before a bounce back.

Thus, the risk-off trend will likely continue through year-end before the crypto sees a 2023-style uptrend.

Final Summary

data.title: MARA stock slides 8% as Bitcoin retreats towards $76,500
data.description:
MARA Holdings shares fell 8.23% to $6.58 during the October 30 session, continuing the decline it’s been seeing in October. The Bitcoin miner’s stock fell as low as $6.44, its lowest level since 2023.

Bitcoin was also trading lower, near $76,714, as MARA’s recent price relationship with it strengthened.

October erases MARA’s September rebound

MARA approached $14 during September before seeing a sharp reversal. At the time of this writing, it had lost more than half its value from that peak.

A recent brief attempt to stay around the $7–$7.50 price area gave way to another decline on Friday. Shares opened at $6.81 and remained below that price at the time of this writing

The session was still underway, leaving the closing price unsettled.

The chart’s moving averages also slope downward above the stock. What this shows is that MARA is trading well below its recent average prices, and its earlier recovery attempts have not helped it to reverse the broader decline.

Bitcoin’s retreat provides context

The comparison chart placed Bitcoin near $76,714 and had reached $76,500 during the ongoing session.

Bitcoin’s decline followed a retreat from around $87,000 in September and early October. The latest selling took it below the $80,000–$82,000 area, where it traded recently.

MARA’s chart showed a 20-period correlation reading of positive 0.78 against BTCUSDT. That indicates a strong positive relationship between their closing-price levels over the selected daily window.

The reading helps to show their recent connection.

Their displayed daily percentage changes also cover different trading windows, since Bitcoin trades continuously and MARA follows stock-market hours.

What would stabilization look like?

Friday’s low of $6.44 would be the first nearby zone MARA should be looking at. If MARA can continue trading below that level, it would extend the decline into new lows. It is worth noting here that MARA share price has not been at the lows we are seeing since March 2023.

If it could push back past $7, then this would be pulling above levels it has been comfortable with lately. Some consolidation in the $7; $7.50 area for the next few days could bring some sense that this most recent slide is losing its steam.

Bitcoin’s nearby reference sits around $76,500, close to its 200-day average. A level to watch if selling does continue is around the 75k low range found in previous sessions.

Both charts still show limited recovery from their latest falls, leaving the next closing prices important to see whether buyers can establish firmer ground.

Final Summary

  • MARA traded at $6.58, down 8.23%, after reaching a fresh low since 2023.
  • Its recent closing-price correlation with Bitcoin was at 0.78 as BTC traded near $76,700.

data.title: Bitwise, Galaxy, and Morpho back CCI’s new framework for U.S crypto vault regulations
data.description:
The Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI) has proposed a new framework to bring crypto vaults under U.S securities laws.

In a 238-page report that was published on 29th October, the CCI outlined how regulators can assess different vault structures under existing securities regulations. This includes the Securities Act of 1933, the Investment Company Act of 1940, and the Investment Advisers Act of 1940.

90-year-old securities rules tested

For those unaware, crypto vaults are smart contracts that accept users’ token deposits and deploy them into financial strategies such as lending, borrowing, and investments to generate returns.

And, now their adoption is expanding beyond decentralized finance (DeFi), with traditional financial institutions also exploring their potential. In fact, according to S&P Global, assets deposited in vaults touched $131 billion in April 2026.

Hence, the CCI, along with members from Bitwise, Galaxy Digital, and Morpho, is arguing that crypto vaults should not automatically fall outside U.S federal securities laws just because they operate via blockchain technology and smart contracts.

Lending more weight to the proposal, Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley said,

Vaults are going to change capital markets. We’re delighted to get to be a part of it.

CCI’s dual framework for crypto vaults

In its detailed report, CCI came up with a two-sided ‘Control Framework’ to resolve how much authority human operators hold over deposited assets. Additionally, the framework would also sort out how much control investors have over their funds.

Additionally, the report examined four factors on the operator’s side, which included mandate, execution, governance, and disposition. Here, the report assessed whether operators can select investment strategies, reallocate capital, change protocol rules, or move deposited assets.

Meanwhile, for the depositor’s side, there were six conditions considered. These included, comprehensibility, verifiability, observability, predictability, notice, and actionability.

So, the crux here is simple, and that is CCI wants vaults with immutable smart contracts, transparent operations, limited human discretion, and permissionless withdrawals to face a different regulatory assessment from those where operators retain significant control over investment decisions.

CCI’s way of bringing regulatory clarity to crypto markets

Interestingly, the proposal also draws parallels with Section 10301 of the proposed CLARITY Act. For those unaware, the latter addressed non-decentralized finance protocols based on whether identifiable individuals or groups could control or materially alter their functionality.

And, therefore, the CCI wants regulators to adopt a similarly control-based approach. In fact, for regulatory clarity, CCI also wants the SEC to follow the approach it previously adopted for ETFs. This would involve granting individual exemptions to qualifying vault structures under Section 6(c) of the Investment Company Act before gradually introducing broader, standardized rules.

Commenting on the same, Horsley added,

We worked with regulators for years to help make crypto ETFs possible. We’re happy to collaborate again, this time on vaults.

The red flag in question

Needless to say, the proposal also echoes SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce’s 22nd July statement, Headstands and Summervaults, in which she cautioned, against treating all crypto vaults alike.

Vaults are not uniform

Here, it’s worth pointing out a recent report by AMBCrypto which highlighted how Web3 protocols are increasingly moving away from their original promises of openness, permissionlessness, and decentralization.

The report stressed on projects such as Hyperliquid, Aave, and Polygon that have adopted models that prioritize internal vaults, buybacks, and treasury accumulation over directly distributing value to token holders.

Final Summary

  • The CCI is arguing that crypto vaults should not automatically fall outside U.S federal securities laws.
  • According to S&P Global, assets deposited in vaults hit $131 billion in April 2026.

data.title: Why AAVE crypto traders must watch $113 support after Binance hack
data.description:
Around 9 pm UTC on the 29th of October, a Binance hot wallet on Ethereum sent 63 ERC-20 tokens and 167,464 ETH in a single transaction. The same exploiter address received another 28,006 ETH in a second transaction from a second Binance hot wallet on Ethereum, along with funds from Arbitrum [ARB], Optimism [OP], and Avalanche [AAVE].

In response, the Aave markets across all networks were frozen, stopping everyone, including the exploiter, from opening new supply or borrow positions.

The broader market has reacted bearishly, with Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] down 3.46% and 3.93% in the past 24 hours, compared to Aave’s 5.67%. The crypto market witnessed over $1.50 billion in liquidations, with a majority being long liquidations.

Is the long-term AAVE trend bullish?

From June to September, the DeFi token rallied by 214.2%, from $60 to $188. Since making this local high, the altcoin has retraced by 32.9% to fall to $125.8.

The weekly trend was bearish, but there is some hope for the bulls that the current retracement could go towards $213-$240, provided the weekly session does not close below $113.4.

Swing traders looking to buy can do so in line with the daily chart, but should remember that the long-term trend was not in their favor.

Why AAVE traders must stay cautious!

The $140 support zone has been breached. The technical indicators on the daily timeframe were firmly bearish. At the same time, the swing structure was just about bullish.

The fair value gap around the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level (white) at $129 was breached, and the bullish order block around $115 was being tested.

If the market-wide selling continues, it is highly likely Aave’s price structure would take a bearish shift. As things stand, swing traders can wait for a sign of demand, maybe in the form of heavy demand or a price move back above $120, to consider going long.

Final Summary

  • The Aave response to the Binance heist was to freeze their v3 and v4 markets, which was effective but also put selling pressure on the DeFi token and other related assets.
  • In this environment of fear, going long is risky. Swing traders can wait for a clearer conditions before looking for trading opportunities.
